acv.quote: Ninety-five K ACV, on a two-year term.

data.reason: The CFO, Martin, decided from a controller's one-pager that compared only per-transaction rates. Nothing on it showed what the failed big-basket orders were costing, so he saw us as 'the same thing' at a higher price after the bank sharpened its rate. Sam blames price, but the real gap was that we never sized the value in Fernbrook's own numbers.

trigger.action: Aim messaging at unexplained checkout failures on high-value orders where the current processor can't say why cards fail.
trigger.quote: She said about one in twelve online orders was failing at the payment step, and it was worse on the big baskets.

decider.action: Build a CFO-facing total-cost comparison covering gateway fees and chargeback staffing, so a rate-only one-pager doesn't make us look like 'the same thing'.
decider.quote: Why would I pay more for the same thing.

competitor.action: Prepare reps to pre-empt an incumbent bank's rate-cut counter by saying early that a better rate leaves the failing orders unfixed.
competitor.quote: After the bank came back, every email was the rate.

message.action: Keep the solutions engineer's explanation of why big-ticket orders get declined, and stop leaning on the generic average-acceptance uplift slide as the value claim.
message.quote: When our solutions engineer, Farah, explained why big-ticket orders get knocked back and what we do about it, Lucy was nodding the whole way.

proof.action: Build a one-page business case template that prices the customer's failed orders from a three-month decline export, for champions to hand the CFO.
proof.quote: Lucy asked once if we had something she could hand Martin. Like a one-page business case.

words.action: Use 'orders dying at the last step' and 'the big baskets' in messaging instead of 'declines' and 'acceptance uplift'.
words.quote: we do all the work to get someone to buy a four-thousand-dollar greenhouse and then the card says no.
